{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-la-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"eed90f43ebdf178ad482fa8d54cff80949e11424740846e21ee840b6749b78ad","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-la-class-std:lineage:14","source_registry_sha256":"8fb2294cb50570a3a0fabb25acba3418dba999eb7dd305cc58b73fdf38975613","source_liveness_sha256":"1105a92b5841d065519de4b7fbea05111880de6d2bb8804066a972d19c63b5a0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Traffic signs and work zones","heading":"Traffic signs and work zones","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"# Traffic signs and work zones

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic-control devices include signs, signals and pavement markings that regulate road traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
A driver must recognize traffic controls promptly and obey regulatory signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Traffic directions given by law-enforcement officers, highway personnel and school crossing guards must be obeyed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
A sign’s shape can indicate its meaning before the driver can read its message. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A02
Recognizing a sign’s color and shape helps a driver adjust speed and driving behavior before reading its words. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A02
The octagon is reserved for stop signs, which require slowing and making a full stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A02
Rectangular regulatory signs can address speed, school zones, parking or loading. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A02
A diamond-shaped sign warns of a hazard or approaching condition. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A02
An orange diamond warns of a construction zone and calls for slower, cautious travel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A02
Yellow diamonds can warn of curves, side roads or changes in traffic flow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
A downward-pointing triangle is reserved for yield signs; slow, observe approaching traffic and be ready to stop when necessary. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
A sideways-pointing triangular sign marks a no-passing zone. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
A white railroad crossbuck is a regulatory sign with the meaning of a yield sign. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
A horizontal rectangle can be used for guidance, some warnings or temporary traffic control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
Route markers can use shapes other than the main stop, yield, warning and regulatory shapes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A03
Red on a stop, yield, do-not-enter or wrong-way sign communicates stopping or a prohibited action. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A03
Orange is a temporary-control background color that warns of construction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A03
Amber warning or school-sign backgrounds call for caution, alertness and readiness to slow. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A03
Black can be the background for one-way, night-speed-limit and truck-regulation signs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A03
Black lettering can appear on white, yellow, orange, fluorescent-pink or fluorescent-yellow-green sign backgrounds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A03
White is used behind most regulatory signs and some route markers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A03
White lettering can appear on red, green, blue, brown or black sign backgrounds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A03
Blue can identify traveler services, information, evacuation routes and portions of some route markers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
Light blue is used for disability-parking signs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
Green backgrounds provide guidance or information, while green wording can indicate permissive regulation or parking. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A03
Fluorescent yellow-green backgrounds identify pedestrian, bicycle and school warnings. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
Brown backgrounds identify guidance for recreational or cultural destinations. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A03
Fluorescent pink backgrounds identify incident-management signs, such as storm-related controls or a crash closure. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A04
Warning signs alert a driver to possible danger, a hazard or a special roadway situation ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A04
A warning may require slowing and being ready to stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A04
Warning signs are usually yellow diamonds with black lettering or symbols. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A04
Some school-zone, school-crossing and pedestrian-crossing warnings use fluorescent yellow. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A05
Regulatory signs communicate laws governing traffic direction, lane use, turns, speed, parking or another special situation. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A05
A red circle and red slash over a symbol prohibit the depicted action. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A06
A speed-limit sign may specify the maximum legal speed or a required minimum speed. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A06
A posted maximum is appropriate only for ideal conditions, and weather, traffic or limited visibility can require a lower speed. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A06
The school-zone speed on a School Speed Limit When Flashing sign applies while the lights flash; otherwise the ordinary roadway limit applies. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A06
Lane-use signs identify permitted travel or turning movements and may stand beside the road or hang over a lane. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A06
Arrows painted on the pavement can supplement lane-use signs. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F40 | anchor: A06
A stop sign is eight-sided, red and lettered in white. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F41 | anchor: A06
At a stop sign, stop behind a provided stop line or crosswalk. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F42 | anchor: A06
After stopping, check all directions and yield to crossing vehicles and pedestrians before entering when safe. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F43 | anchor: A06
An all-way or numbered-way plaque at a stop-controlled intersection indicates that every approaching direction has a stop sign. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F44 | anchor: A06
A yield sign is a red-and-white triangle pointed downward and requires allowing traffic with the right of way to proceed first. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F45 | anchor: A06
A shared center left-turn lane serves left turns from either direction and cannot be used for through travel or passing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F46 | anchor: A06
When making a left turn from the shared center lane, a driver must not travel more than 200 feet within that lane. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]
